material: Polycarbonate housing (Ring does not publish a material spec)
features: Same camera body sells in Battery, Plug-In, Solar, hardwired and PoE versions
Quick Release Battery Pack swaps without unmounting the camera
Low-Light Sight full-colour night view instead of grey infrared
Dual-band Wi-Fi 6 — rare at $100 and rarer still inside Ring's own range
Slots straight into an existing Ring/Alexa household with no new app

specs.maxResolution: 2K, which Ring brands 'Retinal 2K'. Ring publishes the pixel count for the Indoor Cam Plus (2560x1440) but not on the Outdoor Cam Plus spec sheet
specs.powerSource: Quick Release Battery Pack. Plug-In, Solar, hardwired and PoE versions of the same camera are sold at different prices; the PoE adapter alone is $29.99 and the solar panels $39.99-$59.99
specs.batteryLifeClaim: Not published by Ring. Ring states only that its batteries are 'designed to go months between charges under normal conditions'
specs.nightVision: Colour night vision (Ring 'Low-Light Sight') plus infrared
specs.weatherRating: Weather-resistant for outdoor use; Ring does not publish an IP rating for this model
specs.localStorage: None in the camera. Ring Edge local storage needs a Ring Alarm Pro base station and the top Ring Pro plan at $19.99/mo
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Live view, two-way talk and motion notifications. Nothing is recorded or saved, ever
specs.rtspOnvif: No RTSP, no ONVIF, no third-party NVR support

pros: $99.99 buys genuine dual-band Wi-Fi 6 — the eufy kit at four times the price is 2.4GHz only
One camera body, five power options, so you can start on battery and move to PoE without rebuying
Full-colour Low-Light Sight rather than the grey infrared Blink still ships at a similar price
Easiest install and the most polished app of anything here
cons: With no plan it records nothing at all — live view and a push notification is the entire free tier
Ring publishes no battery-life figure for this camera, only that batteries last 'months'
Local storage exists only as Ring Edge, which needs a Ring Alarm Pro base station AND the $19.99/mo Pro plan
No RTSP, no ONVIF, no NVR: the camera is worth nothing outside the Ring app
Ring renamed every plan on 14 January 2026 (Basic became Solo, Standard became Multi), so older price comparisons no longer line up
shortTagline: The easiest $100 camera to live with — and it saves nothing without a plan.

model: Google Nest Cam Indoor, Wired (3rd Gen, GA09973-US)
material: Polycarbonate with a fabric-look base (Google does not publish a material spec)
connectivity: Wi-Fi (Google does not publish the supported bands on the US store listing)
features: 2K HDR sensor Google says takes in 120% more light than the 2nd-gen Nest Cam
Gemini-powered natural-language search across your event history
Free tier doubled from 3 to 6 hours versus the older Nest cameras
Removable magnetic lens cover and a physical mic disable
Ranked #1 for image quality among 2026 indoor cameras by DXOMARK, per Google's listing

specs.powerSource: Wired only — USB-C indoor power adapter. Google notes a cable is needed for 24/7 recording
specs.nightVision: Colour low-light imaging; Google claims 120% more light sensitivity than the 2nd gen
specs.wifiBands: Not published on the US store listing
specs.localStorage: None. No Nest camera has ever had a microSD slot, a hub, or a NAS path
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Live view, alerts, two-way talk, and up to 6 hours of Event Video Previews — 10-second clips, not full event recordings
specs.rtspOnvif: No RTSP, no ONVIF, no NVR support

pros: The best-looking daylight image of any $100 indoor camera here, and it holds colour far lower into dusk
Free tier is genuinely better than Ring's or Arlo's — 6 hours of event previews beats nothing at all
Gemini search across history is the only AI feature in this set that changes how you use the app
Google's 24/7 continuous recording (Advanced plan) is a real capability Ring only sells as a $3/mo add-on
cons: Those free 6 hours are 'Event Video Previews' — 10-second clips, not the event recordings Google's older 3-hour free tier gave
Zero local storage. No card, no hub, no NAS, no offline fallback of any kind
Nest Aware became Google Home Premium in 2025 and the useful tier (Advanced, 60-day history plus 24/7) is $20/mo
Google does not publish the Wi-Fi bands, the frame rate, or the bitrate anywhere on the US listing
Indoor only — the outdoor 2nd-gen wired version is a separate $149.99 purchase
shortTagline: Best picture at $100 indoors, and the only camera here with no local storage at all.

model: Arlo Pro Security Camera 2K HDR, 6th Gen (VMC4070P)
material: Polycarbonate (Arlo does not publish a material spec)
features: Connects straight to your router — no SmartHub required, unlike the Ultra line
USB-C charging replaces the Ultra 2 era magnetic puck
Swappable battery so the camera never comes off the wall to charge
Integrated spotlight drives full-colour night video
Arlo Intelligence AI detection and the Early Warning System alerting layer

specs.powerSource: Swappable rechargeable battery, USB-C charging. Arlo's solar panel charger is a separate $49.99 accessory
specs.batteryLifeClaim: Up to 8 months (Arlo). Arlo publishes no events-per-day assumption behind the figure, and states only that the 6th-gen cell lasts 15% longer than the Pro 5
specs.nightVision: Colour night vision driven by the built-in spotlight, with IR black-and-white as the fallback
specs.weatherRating: Weather-resistant, indoor or outdoor; Arlo does not publish an IP rating on the US product page
specs.wifiBands: Dual-band 2.4GHz and 5GHz straight to the router — no hub needed
specs.localStorage: Only through an Arlo SmartHub (sold separately) with a microSD card you also supply. Nothing records to the camera
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Live view and motion notifications. No cloud clip is ever saved
specs.rtspOnvif: No RTSP, no ONVIF, no third-party NVR support

pros: 8-month battery claim is the longest rechargeable figure here outside eufy's solar cameras
No SmartHub required, which is exactly what separates it from the Ultra 3 sitting above it
Swappable battery plus USB-C means no ladder trip and no proprietary charging puck
160-degree view and 2K HDR make it the sharpest sub-$150 battery camera in this set
cons: Arlo's free tier is the harshest in the category: live view and a notification, and that is all — no recording whatsoever
Local storage needs a SmartHub you buy separately plus a microSD you also buy separately
Arlo Secure Plus for one camera is $9.99/mo, and unlimited cameras is $19.99/mo — the most expensive per-household plan here
No RTSP, no ONVIF: an Arlo is worthless the day Arlo turns the servers off
Arlo does not publish frame rate, bitrate, IP rating or the usage assumption behind the 8-month battery number
shortTagline: Excellent battery camera, brutal subscription: pay nothing and it records nothing.

model: Arlo Ultra Security Camera 4K HDR, 3rd Gen — 2-Cam Kit with SmartHub (VMS5250-100NAS)
material: Polycarbonate (Arlo does not publish a material spec)
features: 180-degree diagonal view — the widest single-lens field in this set
Auto-Zoom and Tracking follows a subject across the frame in 4K
SmartHub in the box gives local microSD recording and longer range
12x digital zoom with dual mics, echo cancellation and wind-noise reduction
USB-C battery and charging, compatible with Arlo XL battery housings

specs.maxResolution: 4K (8 megapixel sensor); 2K, 1080p and 720p modes also offered
specs.topResolutionFrameRate: Not published by Arlo. Trusted Reviews' testing found the 4K Ultra 3 records at the same bitrate as the 2K Pro 6, so the extra pixels are paid for in compression rather than detail
specs.powerSource: Swappable rechargeable battery, USB-C. Only Arlo-certified USB-C or universal solar panels work; the magnetic-base panels do not
specs.batteryLifeClaim: Up to 6 months (Arlo). Trusted Reviews' tester called four months plus more realistic
specs.nightVision: Colour night vision driven by the built-in spotlight, with IR black-and-white fallback. Trusted Reviews measured about a second of colour stabilisation after the light fires
specs.weatherRating: Weather-resistant, indoor or outdoor; Arlo does not publish an IP rating
specs.wifiBands: 2.4GHz and 5GHz, but the camera talks to the SmartHub, which Arlo's own FAQ says is required
specs.localStorage: SmartHub with a microSD card. The hub is in this 2-camera kit; the microSD card is not, and for a single or add-on camera the hub is not either
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Live view and motion notifications only. Arlo's own FAQ confirms cloud storage, interactive notifications and object detection all stop with the trial
specs.rtspOnvif: No RTSP, no ONVIF, no third-party NVR support

pros: 180-degree field of view genuinely removes the blind spots a 140-degree camera leaves at a corner
SmartHub is in the box on this kit, so local microSD recording is a card away rather than a $100 accessory away
Auto-Zoom and Tracking in 4K is the one feature here that no cheaper camera imitates convincingly
USB-C battery and swappable cells mean the camera stays on the wall for its whole life
cons: 4K recording and streaming require Arlo's higher Secure Plus tier — on the base plan you get a 4K camera producing 2K files
Trusted Reviews found the 4K stream runs at the same bitrate as the 2K Pro 6, so 4K here mostly buys compression artefacts
The SmartHub is mandatory. Buy a single Ultra 3 or an add-on camera and it is inert until you also buy a VMB5000
The microSD card is never included, on any Ultra 3 SKU
$349.99 for two cameras before you have paid a cent of subscription, and no plan means no recording
shortTagline: A 4K camera whose 4K is gated behind the pricier plan, and whose hub is not optional.

model: eufy eufyCam S3 Pro 2-Cam Kit with HomeBase 3 (T8892)
material: Polycarbonate with an integrated solar panel on the camera top
features: MaxColor Vision gives full-colour night video with the spotlight off
1/1.8in stacked CMOS behind an f/1.0 lens — the fastest optic in this set
Solar panel built into the camera, not a $30 bolt-on
HomeBase 3 takes a 2.5in SATA drive or SSD up to 16TB with no cloud fee
On-device AI face recognition runs on the hub, not on someone's server

specs.topResolutionFrameRate: Up to 15 fps at 4K, on eufy's own spec sheet
specs.fieldOfView: Not published on eufy's US product page for this model
specs.powerSource: 13,000mAh battery with a solar panel built into the camera. An external panel is a separately sold $29.99 backup for shaded sites
specs.batteryLifeClaim: Up to 365 days, and eufy claims one hour of daily direct sun keeps it charged indefinitely. eufy quantifies it: the built-in panel gathers 450-900mAh a day against 100-200mAh of average daily use
specs.nightVision: MaxColor Vision — full colour with no spotlight, from the 1/1.8in sensor and f/1.0 aperture. Identifies faces and plates to about 30ft in low light
specs.wifiBands: 2.4GHz only (802.11b/g/n). No 5GHz anywhere in this $430 kit
specs.localStorage: HomeBase 3 with 16GB eMMC built in, expandable to 16TB with a 2.5in SATA drive or SSD you supply. One hub handles up to 16 cameras
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Everything. Recording, playback, face recognition and alerts are all local, with no plan at any point
specs.rtspOnvif: No RTSP or ONVIF from the cameras. Apple Home works but caps video at 1080p rather than 4K

pros: The only camera here that produces genuinely usable full colour at night without turning a spotlight on, which is also why its battery lasts
No subscription, ever — recording, AI face recognition and 16TB of expandable local storage are all included in the hardware price
eufy publishes actual solar maths (450-900mAh harvested against 100-200mAh used) instead of the usual 'forever power' hand-waving
IP67 and a 13,000mAh cell: this is the least maintenance-hungry outdoor camera in the set
cons: 4K runs at up to 15 fps — half the frame rate of the UniFi G6 Instant, and eufy prints it in its own specs rather than hiding it
2.4GHz-only Wi-Fi on a $430 kit, when a $99.99 Ring does dual-band Wi-Fi 6
Apple Home users get 1080p, not 4K — the HomeKit path throws away most of what you paid for
No RTSP and no ONVIF, so despite all the local storage the cameras still will not talk to Blue Iris, Frigate or a third-party NVR
The hub is a single point of failure: lose the HomeBase 3 and you lose the recordings on the drive inside it
shortTagline: Best night vision and zero subscription — at 15fps, on 2.4GHz, for $430.

features: 2.5K QHD sensor at a price where 1080p is still normal
Two 72-lumen spotlight LEDs plus four IR LEDs and a 99dB siren
IP65-rated, so it genuinely goes outside despite being a desk-sized cube
microSD recording works with no subscription at all
Free cloud tier still gives 12-second clips and 14 days of history

specs.topResolutionFrameRate: 20 fps by day and 15 fps at night, on Wyze's own tech-spec page
specs.powerSource: Wired micro-USB, 5V/1A. The 6ft cable and adapter in the box are indoor-rated — outdoor mounting needs Wyze's $19.98 Outdoor Power Adapter
specs.nightVision: Colour night vision from a starlight sensor, backed by two 5000K 72-lumen spotlight LEDs and four 850nm IR LEDs
specs.localStorage: microSD up to 256GB in exFAT, continuous or event-based. Card not included; Wyze sells a 32GB card for $18.98
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Live view with no time limit, two-way audio, full microSD recording, plus 12-second cloud clips with 14-day history — but a 5-minute cooldown between cloud clips
specs.rtspOnvif: Not published by Wyze — the Cam v4 tech-spec page lists no RTSP or ONVIF support

pros: Under $40 for 2.5K, IP65, a spotlight, a 99dB siren and a microSD slot — nothing else here comes close on price per feature
Free tier is the most generous in the category: unlimited live view plus real cloud clips, not just notifications
Local microSD recording is unrestricted and needs no plan, unlike Ring, Nest, Arlo or Blink
Wyze actually publishes its frame rates (20fps day, 15fps night), which Ring, Arlo, Nest and TP-Link do not
cons: The free cloud tier's 5-minute cooldown means a burglary that unfolds over ten minutes gets one 12-second clip
Cam Plus annual went from $19.99 to $29.99 per camera in March 2026, a 50% rise
The included adapter and cable are indoor-only — outdoor use quietly costs another $19.98
2.4GHz Wi-Fi only, microSD capped at 256GB, and no card in the box
No RTSP or ONVIF listed, and Wyze's record of app outages and security incidents is a real consideration for a camera in your house
shortTagline: The most camera per dollar anywhere — as long as you never need the free cloud tier.

model: Reolink Argus 4 Pro with Solar Panel 2
features: Two 4mm lenses stitched into one seamless 180-degree image with no centre blind spot
ColorX night vision works at f/1.0 with the spotlight left off
Dual-band Wi-Fi 6 on a battery camera, which is genuinely unusual
6W solar panel bundled in the box rather than sold separately
microSD in the camera and no monthly fee for any core function

specs.maxResolution: 5120x1440 (8MP) — a stitched dual-lens panorama, not a 3840x2160 4K frame, despite the 4K marketing
specs.topResolutionFrameRate: 15 fps at full resolution, on Reolink's own spec sheet
specs.powerSource: 5000mAh built-in (non-removable) battery with a bundled 6W solar panel; USB-A to USB-C charging cable in the box
specs.batteryLifeClaim: Reolink publishes no runtime in days. It claims only '30% More Battery Life' than an IR camera and '+12 Days Standby', plus '10 minutes of charging can power the camera for 24 hours'
specs.nightVision: ColorX full colour at night from an f/1.0 aperture with the spotlight off. Five 2W 6500K spotlights are there if you want them, at a battery cost
specs.localStorage: microSD in the camera. Sources conflict on the ceiling: Reolink's product page says up to 512GB, The Ambient's review says 128GB. A 128GB card ships in some bundles
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Everything. Recording, AI person/vehicle/animal detection and playback are all local and free
specs.rtspOnvif: No standalone RTSP or ONVIF. Reolink's own support article states its battery cameras do 'not support RTSP, RTMP, ONVIF and related communication protocols'; you need the separately sold Reolink Home Hub to expose them

pros: 180 degrees with no stitching seam covers a corner or a driveway that would otherwise need two cameras
ColorX gives usable colour at night without the spotlight, which is the difference between a night image and a battery drain
Dual-band Wi-Fi 6 plus a bundled solar panel plus a 2-year warranty — the best hardware-per-dollar in the battery class
No subscription for anything, and the microSD card lives in the camera rather than in a hub you must buy
cons: The '4K' is 5120x1440 from two stitched lenses at 15 fps — it is a panorama, not a 4K frame, and the vertical field is only 50 degrees
No standalone RTSP or ONVIF: Reolink's own docs confirm battery cameras need the extra-cost Home Hub before any NVR can see them
Reolink publishes no battery runtime figure at all, only relative claims against an unnamed IR camera
Sources conflict on the microSD ceiling — 512GB on Reolink's page, 128GB in The Ambient's review
No Apple HomeKit support, and reviewers consistently describe the Reolink app as cluttered
shortTagline: A 180-degree panorama sold as 4K — brilliant value, so long as you read the fine print.

model: Blink Outdoor 2K+ — 1-Camera System with Sync Module Core
features: Two AA lithium cells included, no charging and no cable for two years
Three quality modes: Best 2K/24fps, Standard 1080p/24fps, Saver 720p/15fps
Sync Module Core included in the box
4x digital zoom and two-way audio with noise cancellation
IP65, rated to -4F, at 142 grams

specs.maxResolution: 2K (2560x1440) in Best mode only; Standard is 1080p and Saver is 720p
specs.topResolutionFrameRate: 24 fps at 2K, 24 fps at 1080p, 15 fps at 720p
specs.powerSource: Two Energizer Ultimate Lithium AA cells, included, non-rechargeable. An optional weather-resistant mains adapter is sold separately
specs.batteryLifeClaim: Up to two years — and Blink's own FAQ says that figure is 'based on battery efficiency settings with 1080p resolution', not the 2K the camera is named after
specs.nightVision: Infrared 850nm. Blink markets 'colour vision in low light', which produces colour at dusk and switches to black-and-white IR in real darkness
specs.wifiBands: 2.4GHz only (802.11ax). Blink specifies 6 Mbps upload for 2K, 3 Mbps for 1080p, 2 Mbps for 720p
specs.localStorage: Possible, but not with anything in this box. The bundled Sync Module Core has no USB port and no card slot. You need a Sync Module 2 ($49.99) plus a USB drive, or a Sync Module XR plus a microSD card — all sold separately, 256GB maximum
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Live view and basic motion alerts once the system is armed. Person and vehicle detection require a Blink plan
specs.rtspOnvif: No RTSP, no ONVIF, no third-party NVR support

pros: Batteries are in the box and the camera is genuinely fit-and-forget for a year or more
Blink is unusually honest in its own FAQ about the resolution the two-year claim assumes
$3.99/mo is the cheapest single-camera plan of any big-brand camera here
A real jump on the Outdoor 4: reviewers report readable licence plates at 2K where 1080p could not
cons: The two-year battery claim is measured at 1080p. Run it in Best mode, which is the only way to get the 2K you paid for, and the figure does not apply
The Sync Module Core in the box cannot do local storage at all — no USB port, no card slot. Local recording means buying a second sync module
Night vision is plain 850nm infrared. 'Colour vision in low light' is dusk colour, not colour after dark
Reviewers report the 2K+ does not work in extended range mode with the XR sync module, so XR owners are stuck on the older Outdoor 4
2.4GHz only, no RTSP, no ONVIF, and person/vehicle detection is paywalled
shortTagline: Two-year battery — measured at 1080p, not at the 2K it is named after.

features: Under $30 for a 2K IP66 camera that works indoors or outdoors
Person, pet and vehicle detection free, with no Tapo Care subscription
RTSP and ONVIF Profile S for Synology, Blue Iris, Frigate or an NVR
Invisible 940nm IR mode alongside the standard 850nm LEDs
9.8ft cable and the power adapter both in the box

specs.topResolutionFrameRate: Not published by TP-Link on the US product page
specs.powerSource: Wired 5V/1A USB adapter with a 3-metre (9.8ft) cable, both included
specs.nightVision: Colour night vision from a starlight sensor plus twin spotlights; 850nm IR to 30ft and an invisible 940nm IR mode
specs.localStorage: microSD up to 512GB. Card not included
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Full local microSD recording plus free person, pet and vehicle detection. Tapo Care cloud storage is genuinely optional
specs.rtspOnvif: RTSP and ONVIF Profile S. TP-Link states that 'most Tapo cameras, except for battery-powered models' support them, though the C120 is not named in its published model list. Profile S carries no two-way audio, a camera account must be enabled first, and only two of {Tapo Care, SD recording, NVR/NAS/ONVIF} can run at the same time

pros: $29.99 for a 2K IP66 camera with a 512GB card slot, free AI detection and RTSP is the best value in the category
One of only three cameras here that will stream to Blue Iris, Frigate, Synology or a generic NVR
Power adapter and a 3-metre cable are both in the box — Wyze charges $19.98 for the outdoor equivalent
The 940nm invisible IR mode means no glowing red ring giving the camera away at night
cons: TP-Link limits you to two of {Tapo Care, SD recording, NVR/ONVIF} at once — you cannot run cloud, card and NVR together
ONVIF is Profile S only, which excludes two-way audio, and RTSP needs a separate camera account enabled in the app
2.4GHz Wi-Fi only, and no frame rate is published anywhere on TP-Link's US page
microSD card is not included, and Tapo's US warranty is 1 year on cameras, not the 2 years buyers often assume
Wired only — there is no battery or PoE option in this model
shortTagline: $30, 2K, IP66 and it speaks RTSP — the budget pick that outlives its own app.

model: Aqara Camera Hub G5 Pro, PoE (CH-C03E)
material: Polycarbonate with a graphite-cooled sensor assembly
features: HomeKit Secure Video over PoE — a combination almost nothing else offers
Doubles as a Zigbee 3.0 hub, Thread border router and Matter controller
Seven visual and four audio AI detections run on the camera, not in a cloud
1/1.8in sensor behind an f/1.0 lens for colour night vision
RTSP plus SMB NAS backup, and ONVIF added by firmware 4.3.4

specs.topResolutionFrameRate: Not published by Aqara on the US product page
specs.powerSource: 802.3af PoE (48V, 0.27A) or USB-C 5V/2A. The box holds a power cable and an RJ45 waterproof kit — no PoE injector and no PoE switch
specs.batteryLifeClaim: Not applicable — PoE or mains powered
specs.nightVision: Colour night vision from a 1/1.8in sensor at f/1.0, with a 3W 3000K spotlight available if you want it
specs.wifiBands: Dual-band 2.4GHz and 5GHz with WPA3 on the Wi-Fi model; this PoE model can use Ethernet instead. Also carries Zigbee 3.0 and Thread radios
specs.localStorage: 8GB encrypted eMMC on board plus SMB NAS backup, or HomeKit Secure Video. There is no microSD slot
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Everything. All seven AI detections run on the camera and recording goes to eMMC, your NAS or HomeKit Secure Video with no plan
specs.rtspOnvif: RTSP and SMB NAS from launch; ONVIF added in firmware 4.3.4, which Aqara confirmed publicly and which lets UniFi Protect adopt it as a third-party camera

pros: The most open camera here: RTSP, ONVIF, SMB NAS, HomeKit Secure Video, Alexa, Google, SmartThings and Matter all at once
Being a Zigbee hub and Thread border router as well means it replaces a $60-$100 hub you would otherwise buy
f/1.0 over a 1/1.8in sensor gives colour at night without leaving a spotlight on, at half eufy's price
PoE means one cable for power and data, and it runs from -30C, the widest temperature range in this set
cons: PoE injector and switch are not included — budget another $20-$40 unless you already own PoE infrastructure
8GB of eMMC and no microSD slot: without a NAS or HomeKit Secure Video your on-camera history is measured in hours
2688x1520 is 4MP, noticeably short of the 4K on the Lorex and UniFi cameras at similar money
Aqara publishes no frame rate or bitrate for the camera anywhere on its US page
ONVIF arrived by firmware update, so a unit on old firmware will not be adopted by a third-party NVR until you update it
shortTagline: HomeKit Secure Video over PoE with RTSP and ONVIF — the least locked-in camera here.

model: Lorex 4K Smart Security Lighting Deterrence Bullet AI PoE Camera (E895AB)
features: 16.7-million-colour deterrence lighting plus an onboard siren
True 3840x2160 single-sensor 4K, not a stitched panorama
Smart Motion Detection Plus for person, vehicle, face, animal and package
IP67 metal body rated -30C to +60C
No monthly fees of any kind — Lorex states it outright

specs.topResolutionFrameRate: 15 fps at 4K. You only get 30 fps by dropping to 5MP, per Lorex's own E895AB datasheet
specs.fieldOfView: 127 degrees diagonal, from a 2.8mm f/1.6 fixed lens
specs.powerSource: 802.3af PoE or 12V DC, 9.5W maximum. An Ethernet extension cable is in the box; no PoE injector, no PoE switch and no 12V adapter
specs.nightVision: Colour Night Vision with a customisable 16.7-million-colour deterrence light, falling back to infrared black-and-white to 98ft when ambient light runs out
specs.localStorage: microSD slot on the camera, or a Lorex Fusion NVR sold separately. Lorex does not publish a card-size ceiling for this model, and card contents are reachable only through the camera's own web interface, not the NVR or the mobile app
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Everything. Lorex's page says it plainly: 'No Monthly Fees. Own it. No subscriptions required'
specs.rtspOnvif: Not published — ONVIF and RTSP appear nowhere in Lorex's E895AB datasheet or product page, although Lorex sells a separate ONVIF-branded professional range

pros: A real single-sensor 4K frame rather than the stitched 5120x1440 panorama Reolink markets as 4K
Metal IP67 body rated -30C to +60C — the toughest housing in this set
No subscription for anything, and Lorex says so on the product page instead of burying it
The colour deterrence light is a genuine deterrent rather than just a night-vision aid
cons: 4K runs at 15 fps. 30 fps only exists if you drop to 5MP, and it is in Lorex's own datasheet
PoE injector, PoE switch and 12V adapter are all missing from the box — you need existing PoE gear or another purchase
ONVIF and RTSP are not published for this model, so 'PoE camera' does not automatically mean it will join your Blue Iris or Frigate setup
microSD recordings can only be pulled through the camera's own browser interface, not the NVR or the app
Lorex does not publish a microSD size ceiling, and Amazon stock for this SKU is intermittent — lorex.com is the reliable channel
shortTagline: Genuine 4K on a tough PoE body — at 15fps, and the injector is not in the box.

features: True 4K at 30fps from a 1/1.8in 8MP sensor — the only camera here doing both
On-camera AI engine with face and licence-plate recognition, no cloud and no fee
Palm-sized body that mounts anywhere within reach of a USB-C outlet
Joins an existing UniFi Protect system in minutes over Wi-Fi
UniFi Protect now also adopts ONVIF third-party cameras, so the console is not single-vendor

specs.topResolutionFrameRate: 30 fps at 4K, per Ubiquiti's own tech specs — the highest full-resolution frame rate in this set
specs.powerSource: 5V/2A USB-C adapter included with a 2-metre cable, 7W maximum. A PoE-to-USB-C adapter is a separate purchase
specs.nightVision: Infrared only, and Ubiquiti rates it to just 6m (20ft) — the shortest published IR range here. No colour night mode
specs.weatherRating: IPX5 and IK04 — splash-resistant, with no dust rating at all. Rated -20C to +40C
specs.wifiBands: Wi-Fi 5 (802.11a/b/g/n/ac) plus Bluetooth. No Wi-Fi 6 on a 2025 camera
specs.localStorage: Ubiquiti's tech specs list a microSD card slot, but recording is designed to land on a UniFi Protect console. Sources conflict: iFeeltech's hands-on review states the G6 Instant has no microSD support
specs.noSubscriptionBehaviour: Everything, and there is no subscription to buy — but only once you own a UniFi Protect console. The cheapest is the UNVR Instant at $199, so the real entry cost is about $378
specs.rtspOnvif: The camera is adopted only by a UniFi Protect console and does not speak ONVIF outward to a third-party NVR. Ubiquiti does not list RTSP or ONVIF in the G6 Instant tech specs

pros: The only camera here that delivers 4K at 30fps rather than 4K at 15 or 20fps
Face and licence-plate recognition run on the camera with no monthly fee, forever
Genuinely fast to deploy — installers report a dozen units in under four hours on an existing UniFi network
Once you own a console there is no recurring cost at all, which pays back a Ring or Arlo plan inside two years
cons: It does nothing on its own. Every UniFi Protect camera needs a console — the cheapest is a $199 UNVR Instant, taking the real price to about $378
IPX5 with no dust rating and a -20C to +40C range: this is a sheltered-porch camera, not an exposed-wall one
IR night vision to only 6m (20ft), with no colour night mode, against eufy and Reolink doing full colour at 30ft
Wi-Fi 5 in 2025, and 4K recording eats 50-60GB of console storage per camera per week
Sources conflict on whether the microSD slot Ubiquiti lists is actually usable, and Ubiquiti publishes no RTSP or ONVIF output
shortTagline: Real 4K30 with no subscription — after you have bought the $199 console it needs.
